_[CONCLUDED 2.5.21 – SCROLL TO BOTTOM OF POST]_

Hi everyone, firstly I'd just like to introduce myself. I'm Sean and I am currently working on the new brand identity for Edgeware. You can view the brief [here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11vCC-bO0F_-0wGXx1FmaD95N4lQHcCY2-QRgx1YxYhg/edit)

It's been an extremely interesting and informative journey so far and I’m pleased to share some initial updates with you on where we are at with the project, so here goes…

The process started by taking all of the market research, existing creative, new narrative development and vision for Edgeware and distilling this down into key areas of interest and succinct insights that would form the base of the thinking and conceptual development of the brand...

![](https://commonwealth-uploads.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/0661f9ea-0e5b-4b64-a267-aa7a8fc664de.1612196564821)


These key insights led me into determining what exactly they could mean and look like if we were to visualise them. Essentially, how could we communicate these terms in a simple standalone image...

![](https://commonwealth-uploads.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/897c3c58-d60d-4d30-96c6-428c03dcf2b7.1612197928602)


At this point, the thought process moved slightly retrospectively – looking at the existing Edgeware creative and assessing the merits of the concepts being symbolised...

![](https://commonwealth-uploads.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/9e4975cc-d321-48c3-8859-6d4262fc4958.1612198158479)


There felt like a real opportunity to explore these further, not necessarily just from a visual perspective but more conceptually. Something really interesting was resonating with me in the forms that symbolised individual elements coming together to form a solid, meaningful connection. Not only that, but the idea of taking a step back to see the bigger picture – realising that the whole is greater than the sum of its parts. But what if in Edgeware’s case, these parts (or collectives) play their own important role just as much as the next one in allowing creative freedom? And that ultimately great things can happen within each self-governing, polycultural entity, as well as across the whole Edgeware community.

These thoughts began to form the foundation for my initial visual exploration. How do we translate the above into a memorable and distinct mark or visual system? Is it a blank canvas or is there something worth exploring in the existing symbology? The very early stage explorations focused on the latter – seeing how the forms in the current logo could be developed...

![](https://commonwealth-uploads.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/ac767ead-8cbd-4e11-8a4d-e9f4471dbc2e.1612198205767)


Some interesting forms were taking shape, particularly those that felt organic and like they were evolving. The feeling like elements dissipating from a central source. Something to explore further. However are the above strong enough? Do they convey the ideas of providing the building blocks for the future? Of true creative freedom? Further exploration took me down an avenue focussed around clear individual elements that had potential to take on a life of their own whilst remaining part of something far greater...

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)


This was where I felt somewhat of a ‘lightbulb’ moment. Not just visually, but conceptually, this territory felt right. Edgeware provides the foundations and the tools to create, to build, to connect, to revolutionise and to be apart of something worthwhile.

But without getting too far ahead, some further exploration and development was needed. So I picked out 3 concepts of interest that were worth expanding upon...

![](https://commonwealth-uploads.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/129c31a1-bfed-4a6f-9c80-5a03d67ac29e.1612198818393)


The first is an evolution of the existing Edgeware symbols. It feels dynamic and recognisable as representing communities and as a nexus bringing ideas together. 

Second is a bold and optically striking geometric form that represents an accessible, powerful and dynamic network. Almost like a gravitational pull bringing everything to its core.

The third is born out of a similar structure to the existing symbols, this represents the building blocks for the future. The simple 3D blocks can take on a life of their own whilst always being able to form back together to create something stronger.

Things are taking shape (literally) but nothing quite feels tangible as a brand identity and visual system. So the next stage was to start developing the concepts further, which leads to the final batch of progress shots. So I began expanding on concept 3 first, exploring how it could evolve and become more than just a static mark. How a visual system could start to organically form and bring the brand narrative to life...

![](https://commonwealth-uploads.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/10c7a02f-391b-4558-8cec-4065308b182d.1612198449544)
![](https://commonwealth-uploads.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/50230e1c-37a4-4504-ade8-4068280053b3.1612198467912)

And that is where the pause button has been pressed. Things to note are that further development of each concept is needed of course and that colour palettes and additional assets will be tested further along the line. Up to this point it’s much more about nailing down the concept and the foundations of the potential graphic system.


I now leave the floor open for you all to give your thoughts, feelings and feedback so far. I know this sort of thing can be subjective and open to interpretation but hopefully the narrative has helped explained why certain decisions have been made and the process that has led to this current point. We will collate and review feedback from the community over the coming days that will inform further development :) 

Thanks everyone!
